intelligence.human_view: A runner who keeps restarting the race never crosses the finish line — and a page that keeps coming back not good is a race restarted. The finish line breaks the redo loop with the whole-page rule: Personal lands whole first, then the Hub, then the Dashboard, then Membership — each whole, no new scope until one lands. A page is not done because a round finished; it is done because he saw the whole page, on his screen, and it held. And the frame that holds the pages is not a description — he made it with his own hands, and said "use this one." To extend it down a longer interface, repeat the centre metal pattern — never stretch it, because stretching would warp the seals and the centre N. The pattern repeats, the architecture holds.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you have four puzzles to finish — first the Personal puzzle, then the Hub, then the Dashboard, then the Membership. You finish one whole puzzle before you start the next one — no starting a new puzzle until the first one is done! And the golden frame around the puzzles is one Dad made himself — you use his frame, exactly as he made it. If you need a longer frame, you repeat the middle pattern — never stretch it, or it would bend.
